newsitem.title: USA: Search launched for hikers missing in Arizona.
newsitem.headline: Search launched for hikers missing in Arizona.

text.p: A search was launched early on Wednesday for 11 hikers, many of them Europeans, reported missing when an 11-foot (3.3 metre) wall of water crashed down on them in a narrow canyon in northern Arizona, authorities said.

Rescuers combed the normally dry upper Antelope Canyon, about 50 miles (80 km) north-east of the Grand Canyon, following a flash flood that roared through the area on Tuesday, creating an "11-foot wall of water," Capt. Rex Stermer, operations chief for the Coconino Sheriff's Office, said.
Five of those missing were part of a tour group organized by TrekAmerica, a Los Angeles company that provides excursions nationwide for foreign visitors.
The missing included tourists from France, Britain and Sweden, Stermer said.
Authorities said tour guide Poncho Quintana escaped the floodwaters and was taken to a local hospital. He was not believed to be seriously injured.
John Peluso, an assistant manager for TrekAmerica, told Reuters the hikers had gone into the canyon to take photographs when the flood hit.

"It's a very popular place for photographs. It is run by the Navajo Indians who charge an entrance fee. It is known as a slot canyon, the walls are very high and only about five feet (1.5 metres) apart. It really is quite spectacular but because it is so narrow it is not the place to be when a flash flood hits," he said.
Northern Arizona has been hit by a number of flash floods in recent days, with tourists and residents being forced to evacuate the Havasupai Indian Reservation earlier this week.
